simple.meaning: סָעַד (çâʻad) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to support (mostly figurative).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 12 times across Genesis, Judges, 1 Kings, Psalms, Proverbs, and 1 more, beginning at Genesis 18:5. Its contexts include family, family line, offering, Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סָעַד (H5582).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: סָעַד (çâʻad) / H5582 is traced through Genesis 18:5, Judges 19:5, Judges 19:8, 1 Kings 13:7 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: I will get a piece of bread so you can refresh your heart. After that you may go your way, now that you have come to your servant.”

majorEvents.label: Birth or introduction
majorEvents.evidenceText: For a child is born to us. A son is given to us; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

timeline.evidenceText: I will get a piece of bread so you can refresh your heart. After that you may go your way, now that you have come to your servant.”

On the fourth day, they got up early in the morning, and he rose up to depart. The young lady’s father said to his son-in-law, “Strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread, and afterward you shall go your way.”
He arose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart; and the young lady’s father said, “Please strengthen your heart and stay until the day declines;” and they both ate.
The king said to the man of God, “Come home with me, and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward.”
You have enlarged my steps under me,
I said, “Yahweh, have mercy on me!
When I said, “My foot is slipping!”
wine that makes the heart of man glad,
Hold me up, and I will be safe,
Love and faithfulness keep the king safe.
For a child is born to us. A son is given to us; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

definitions.full: H5582. saad סָעַד verb support, sustain, stay (Late Hebrew id. , especially take a meal ; Aramaic סְעַד support, stay ; Zinjirli סעד strengthen Lzb 330 , support , perhaps feed Cook 85 ; Christian-Palestinian Aramaic noun aid , Schw Idioticon 64 ; Arabic , III, IV. aid, assist , Lane 1360 , forearm Id 1362 ; Sabean סעד DHM Südar. Ait. p. 16 ); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular וְסָעַד consecutive Prov 20:28 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִסְעָ֑ד 3feminine singular suffix תִּסְעָדֵ֫נִי Psa 18:36 , read also in || 2Sam 22:36 , etc.; Imperative masculine singular סְעָד Judg 19:5 (on ָ probably © by error, see Kö i. 261 f. GFM on the passage ), סְעָדנָֿא 19:8 (compare id. ), וּסֳעָ֑דָה 1Kin 13:7 ; suffix סְעָדֵנִי Psa 119:117 ; Infinitive construct suffix וּלְסַעֲדָהּ Isa 9:6 ; — support, sustain , always figurative: 1 sustain, stay , the heart (compare לֵבָב 8 , לֵב 8 ), with food Gen 18:5 (J), Judg 19:5 (c. 2 accusative), 19:8 , Psa 104:15 ; object omitted 1Kin 13:7 . 2. a. support throne (subject king) Prov 20:28 , coming ruler Isa 9:6 . b. support, uphold with accusative of person (subject ׳י , his hand etc.) Psa 18:36 + || 2Sam 22:36 (v above ), Psa 20:3 ; 41:4 ; 94:18 ; 119:117 .
